items.title: Formal smoothness for adic topologies follows from formal smoothness, and the discrete variant
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma compares formal smoothness in the sense of the earlier algebraic definition with formal smoothness for adic topologies: the former implies the latter for any linear topology on the source and any pre-adic topology on the target making the map continuous, and for two adic topologies the condition can be checked with the discrete topology on the source. Both directions are continuity bookkeeping around the lifting property: a solid diagram with continuous structure map is turned into a lifting problem for the algebraic notion, and the resulting lift is shown to be continuous by computing that a suitable power of the adic ideal maps into the square-zero kernel, with the converse handled by the symmetric computation of powers of the two ideals.
